beats.care: When factories pay more, phones, clothes, snacks and travel can cost more later. It also pressures RBI to keep loan rates high.
beats.what: Wholesale prices in September were 11.39% higher than a year earlier, up from 9.92% in August, government data showed on 14 October.
beats.why: Fuel and power costs rose nearly 26%, and crude oil and natural gas over 57%. Food, metals and chemicals also got costlier.

cards.title: How much prices rose in a year (Sept)

cards.body: CPI, or retail inflation, tracks what you pay at shops. It was 5.54% in September. WPI tracks what businesses pay for raw materials and goods. RBI targets CPI, but a high WPI is an early warning of what may reach shops.
cards.title: wpi vs cpi: what's the difference?

cards.body: That covers the whole first half of this financial year, so September isn't a one-month blip.
cards.caption: Average wholesale inflation, April–Sept 2026

cards.body: Electricity is the odd one out: its wholesale price actually fell 0.43% from a year ago, while every other kind of fuel got costlier.

cards.q: What's hurting your wallet most lately?

opts: Businesses' higher costs often reach shop prices
cards.q: Why does high wholesale inflation matter to ordinary buyers?
cards.why: WPI tracks what businesses pay; when that rises, firms often pass the extra cost on to customers.

hook: Wholesale prices just jumped *11.39%*. What does that mean for you?

learn.t: Wholesale inflation tracks prices businesses pay each other, before goods reach shops, so it often hints where shop prices are heading.
